{"title":"Fix invoice totals off by one cent","brief":"Owner report: some invoice totals are off by a cent. Requested result: invoice totals are exact to the cent for every line, and the owner can trust the totals shown.

Likely cause (verify first): src/invoices/index.ts `lineTotalCents` does `Math.floor(line.unitPrice * 100) * line.quantity`. Floating-point prices such as 0.29, 1.15, 4.35, 19.99 multiply to values like 28.999999..., so Math.floor drops a cent, and the error is then multiplied by quantity.

What to do:
1. Reproduce first: add failing unit tests in src/invoices/index.test.ts with prices known to break floor (e.g. 0.29, 1.15, 4.35, 8.20, 19.99, 0.07) and quantities > 1, plus a multi-line invoice. Confirm they fail on the current code.
2. Fix the conversion to integer cents so it is exact (e.g. Math.round(unitPrice * 100), or convert via string/decimal parsing). Keep all arithmetic in integer cents after conversion. Check nothing else in src (e.g. src/web/server.ts invoice page) reintroduces float rounding errors on display.
3. Run the full checks: `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser` (tests/browser/invoices.spec.ts). Fix any lint, test failure or flakiness you see.
4. Add an entry to CHANGELOG.md (CI runs `npm run check:changelog` and fails without it).

Constraints: dates in the UI are always DD/MM/YYYY - do not change invoiceDate behaviour. Never run scripts/owner-only.sh; the owner runs it. Follow the project's git policy for this thread.

Report back: root cause confirmed, the failing-then-passing test cases, and output summary of lint/unit/browser checks.","type":"fix","goalId":"goal_78776a45f1d2c050f91104118ed00b3d9d2f6c4c","now":false,"after":[],"needs":[],"fixed":{},"source":"owner-request"}

{"title":"Add CSV export to the customers page","brief":"Owner request: add a CSV export to the customers page. Requested result: on /customers the owner sees an export control and gets a downloaded CSV file of the customers that opens correctly in a spreadsheet.

Context: src/web/server.ts serves /customers as an HTML table (Name, VAT) from the store in src/customers/index.ts (Customer = id, name, vat, createdAt ISO string). There is also /api/customers returning JSON.

What to build:
1. A CSV endpoint (e.g. /customers.csv or /customers/export.csv - note `/customers` currently matches via startsWith, so route the CSV path before it) returning `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="customers.csv"` (a dated filename is fine).
2. Columns: Name, VAT, Created. Created must be formatted DD/MM/YYYY (project rule: dates in the UI are always DD/MM/YYYY). Header row first.
3. Proper CSV escaping per RFC 4180: quote fields containing comma, quote, CR or LF; double embedded quotes. Guard against CSV/formula injection (cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR get a leading apostrophe). Use CRLF line endings; consider a UTF-8 BOM so Excel reads accented names correctly.
4. A clearly visible "Export CSV" link/button on the customers page (text label, no emoji), styled consistently with the existing page. Check the page looks right at desktop and mobile widths.
5. Put the CSV building in a pure, unit-tested function (e.g. in src/customers) - tests for escaping, injection guard, empty list, date format. Add a browser test in tests/browser/customers.spec.ts that clicks the export control and verifies the downloaded file content.
6. Run `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`. Fix any lint, test failure or flakiness you see.
7. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry (CI `npm run check:changelog` requires it).

Constraints: never run scripts/owner-only.sh; the owner runs it. Follow the project's git policy for this thread.

Report back: endpoint path, sample of the CSV output, check results, and a screenshot or description of the page with the export control.","type":"feature","goalId":"goal_af6d33b02368eeaa04a576ad2ffb12fbb166bfb6","now":false,"after":[],"needs":[],"fixed":{},"source":"owner-request"}
